agency: City of Dallas Planning and Development Department (formerly Development Services Department)

code_edition.value: 2023 National Electrical Code (Chapter 56, Dallas Electrical Code, with Dallas amendments)
code_edition.quote: That Chapter 56, “Dallas Electrical Code,” of the Dallas City Code, as amended, is amended by adopting the 2023 Edition of the National Electrical Code of the National Fire Protection Association, Inc.

who_may_file.conditions: Residential homesteaded property only; homeowner must reside in the property, perform all work without hired assistance, pass a homeowner's exam, and have the district electrical inspector witness the exemption form at the field office
who_may_file.quote: For electrical permits, the witness will be the district electrical inspector. Permit must be issued at the field office.

requirements.item: Confirmed city inspection sent to Oncor New Construction Management Center (NCMC) on the ESID account before meter installation
requirements.quote: City must send in a confirmed city inspection to Oncor's New Construction Management Center (NCMC) at c3ncmc@oncor.com or Fax: 888.222.9716 on the previously provided ESID account.

requirements.item: Interconnection agreement, single-page flattened PDF layout sketch, and one-line diagram (<2MB) for residential solar/battery/generator
requirements.quote: Each Diagram must be a single page, completely flattened and non-editable, PDF, less than 2MB.

requirements.item: Visible Lockable Labeled AC Disconnect (VLLD) with external handle on accessible exterior wall within 10 feet of Oncor meter
requirements.quote: The Visible Lockable Labeled AC Disconnect must be located on an ACCESSIBLE, EXTERIOR wall within 10 feet of the Oncor Meter.

requirements.item: Generator interconnection one-line must confirm automatic transfer switch (ATS) mode of operation (open or closed transition)
requirements.quote: If a Generator is connected, please confirm the ATS mode of operation- Open transition or Close transition.

open_questions: Whether standalone contractor-pulled single-family electrical permits (EV charger, service upgrade, subpanel, 240 V appliance circuit) are exempt from plan submittal; opening Section 301.4.7.6 ('Alternative provisions') of https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/DCH%20documents/Chapter%2052%20as%20of%203-27-24.pdf and the Residential Electrical Permit workflow in DallasNow (https://aca-prod.accela.com/DALLASTX) would settle this (note: Chapter 56 Section 81.3(A) requires homestead homeowners doing their own work to file approved plans and specifications).

Minimum/maximum drawing sheet size specifically for standalone electrical and backup generator plan submittals (other Dallas residential checklists such as SOLARPANELWATERHEATEROROTHERSYSTEM.pdf and Single_Family_Dwelling_Remodel.pdf state 11x17 minimum to 36x48 maximum, but the full text of https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/DCH%20documents/BACKUP%20GENERATOR%20PERMIT-updateJ.pdf and https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/DCH%20documents/ELECTRICAL%20PERMIT%20APPLICATION%20CHECKLIST%20updateJ.pdf needs to be opened to confirm whether the same sheet-size note appears there).

Signature or professional seal exemptions for single-family electrical and backup generator plans; opening Section 301.4.7.4.3 ('Plans exempted from engineer's seal') of https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/DCH%20documents/Chapter%2052%20as%20of%203-27-24.pdf and the glossary entry on https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/guide/Pages/default.aspx would settle this.

The exact effective date of City of Dallas's adoption of the 2023 NEC (Chapter 56) could not be confirmed verbatim from the indexed excerpts of https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/DCH%20documents/adopt%202023%20National%20Electrical%20Code%20w%20edits.pdf; meanwhile https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/Pages/electrical_section.aspx still displays 'effective June 13, 2022' above '2023 National Electrical Code'.

No dedicated City of Dallas single-family residential permit checklist or official webpage was found for standalone Level 2 EV chargers, main panel/service upgrades, subpanels, or 240 V appliance circuits (hot tubs, saunas, heat pumps) on dallascityhall.com.

The City of Dallas Forms By Department page (https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/Pages/formsdept.aspx) notes 'Backup Generator Permit (revised on web April 2025)', but the indexed PDF (https://dallascityhall.com/departments/sustainabledevelopment/buildinginspection/DCH%20documents/pdf/BI_Backup%20Generator%20Permit_Rev%2009-11-2018.pdf) is dated REV 09-11-2018; the April 2025 PDF could not be opened directly.

No City of Dallas-published residential electrical load calculation worksheet, mandatory NEC 220 method (220.82 vs. 220.83 vs. 220.87), EV charger service load factor, or minimum plan sheet size was found on dallascityhall.com.

local_rules.quote: Do not apply for a stand alone electrical permit online. It will be cancelled and you will waste your time and money.
